newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Solvay strengthens position in U.S. plastics.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Solvay strengthens position in U.S. plastics.

text.p: Belgian chemicals group Solvay SA said on Tuesday it bought the 50 percent in D&S Plastics International owned by Dexter Corp of the U.S., taking its stake in D&S to 100 percent.
D&S Plastics, headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, is the largest supplier of engineered polyolefin materials to the North American car industry. The plastics are used mainly for car bumpers.
Solvay aims to turn D&S Plastics into a global supplier of car materials, which the group sees as a core business, and said it was determined to strengthen its automotive business further.
Solvay gave no details of the purchasing agreement, which was signed earlier on Tuesday. D&S Plastics has a staff of 300 and sales of some $100 million.

A Solvay spokesman said sales growth was on the cards. D&S Plastics has market share of 50 percent in the Nafta countries -- the U.S., Canada and Mexico. The Belgian group employs more than 35,000 people. It had 1996 turnover of $8.8 billion.
Wall Street-listed Dexter Corp supplies specialty materials to the aerospace, electronics, food packaging and medical markets. It had 1996 sales of $1.1 billion.
